name: Magalu and KaBuM! Push Back the Clock-In
body: Brazilian retailers Magazine Luiza (Magalu) and KaBuM! told staff at both companies they could start work at 11 a.m. Brasília time on launch day instead of the usual hour. KaBuM!'s CEO said it was easier to give everyone a later start than fight the excuses employees would invent to skip work anyway.

name: Pocketpair's "Business Trip to Vice City"
body: Palworld developer Pocketpair gave staff five days of special paid leave from November 19-23, jokingly filing it as a business trip to Vice City. Because the span includes a weekend, it only cost the studio three actual leave days — the second time Pocketpair has granted leave for a rival game's launch.

name: The Paid Course That's Secretly GTA6
body: A German provider built a state-recognized Bildungsurlaub (paid educational leave) course called "Open World Games: Lessons from a Digital World," using GTA6 as the curriculum. It let workers in 12 of Germany's 16 states take three paid days off for a 119-euro fee — all 60 spots filled.

name: A Vienna Firm's Two Paid Days Off
body: Vienna-based electrical engineering company Tudi Elektrotechnik gave its roughly 80 employees two fully paid days off, November 19-20, specifically to play GTA6 — confirmed by the company, and not deducted from anyone's vacation.

name: Burger Motorsports Pauses Operations
body: California auto-parts maker Burger Motorsports announced it would pause company-wide operations on launch day after multiple employees asked for the day off, rather than handle each request individually. Normal operations would resume once staff had "completed their initial exploration" of the game.

name: Edison Motors' Four-Day Weekend
body: Canadian truck manufacturer Edison Motors gave its entire staff November 19-20 off, joking that operations would resume once everyone finished "stealing cars, fleeing law enforcement... in Vice City."

name: G FUEL Cuts Its Store Hours
body: Gaming-energy-drink brand G FUEL shortened its operating hours around launch week specifically so its own staff could go play.

name: The Government's Official Leave-Rights Guidance
body: Australia's Fair Work Ombudsman, a federal regulator, published official guidance explaining workers' rights to request annual leave for GTA6's launch day — and warning there's no statutory entitlement to it, so employers can still say no.

name: "Here's How Not to Break the Law"
body: National broadcaster TVNZ's 1News ran an explainer titled "Want the day off to play GTA6? Here's how not to break the law," walking viewers through lawfully requesting leave and warning that faking a sick day could mean discipline.

name: Parliament Debates the GTA6 Delay
body: A Polish politician raised GTA6's release delay on the floor of Poland's parliament, calling it "a huge scandal" — turning a video game's schedule into a point of national debate.

name: A Minister on Not "Puffing Out Our Chests"
body: A UK government minister said Britain likely won't publicly celebrate GTA6 the way France promoted Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, since most of the game's ownership and revenue sits with Rockstar's US parent — despite GTA6 being largely British-made.

name: Edinburgh Council Backs Rockstar Staff
body: Edinburgh's city council passed a motion backing Rockstar North employees amid an alleged labor dispute at the studio — a local government formally weighing in on how a video game studio treats its own staff.

name: Miami-Dade Rejects a "Vice City" Marketing Deal
body: Miami-Dade County reportedly discussed a marketing deal with GTA6's publisher covering billboards, "Welcome to Vice City" airport signage, and a GTA6-wrapped Metromover train. The county's sheriff publicly opposed it, calling GTA "a video game franchise built around criminal activity."

name: The Army's Re-Enlist-for-GTA6 Pass
body: A memo reportedly circulating from a US Army battalion at Fort Stewart, Georgia, offered any of its 130 eligible soldiers a four-day pass to play GTA6 if they re-enlisted by November 14. A follow-up report said 20 soldiers had signed up by the deadline — though the Army never officially confirmed the memo.

name: Free Copies for Launch-Day Babies
body: Norwegian electronics retailer Komplett offered a free copy of GTA6 to any customer who has a baby on the game's November 19 release date.

name: Midnight Launch Events Across Dubai
body: A UAE retailer ran midnight local-time launch events across its Dubai stores for GTA6's physical release, drawing crowds at the stroke of launch day.

name: Is Dating a Game Character Cheating?
body: UAE residents publicly debated whether romancing an in-game GTA6 character counts as cheating on a real partner — a debate serious enough that a national newspaper covered it.

name: The "Los Santos to Vice City" Boarding Pass
body: One wife marked her husband's GTA6 pre-order by making him a mock boarding pass, departing "Los Santos" and arriving in "Vice City."

name: Kai Cenat's Marathon Streams
body: Streamer Kai Cenat warmed up for launch by streaming all five mainline GTA games back-to-back over roughly 130 hours, then announced he'd stream GTA6 from the moment it launched without stopping until he'd 100%-completed it, optional content included.

name: A YouTuber Tries to Walk Into Rockstar's HQ
body: A German YouTuber and film crew traveled to Rockstar North's Edinburgh studio and tried to film their way inside. Police responded, took their details, and issued a warning, though no crime was found.

name: Drones and Fake IDs at Rockstar North
body: Fans reportedly flew drones past Rockstar North's office windows and tried using fake IDs to get inside, all chasing an early glimpse of the game.

name: The Fan "Monitoring Oxygen Levels" at Rockstar HQ
body: One especially dedicated fan claimed to be tracking oxygen levels and acoustic noise from the bushes outside Rockstar North's headquarters, insisting the readings proved a new trailer was imminent.

name: The "Can I Play GTA6 on My ___" Trend
body: A viral TikTok trend had people jokingly asking whether GTA6 could run on absurd hardware — air fryers, pets, anything but an actual console or PC.

name: The Counterfeit Disc Scam
body: A mobile phone shop in Bangladesh claimed to already be selling physical GTA6 discs years before release, sparking viral mockery once gamers pointed out the game hadn't even come out yet.
